title: Why are Imran Khan's sisters still detained?
credits: Photos: Unsplash (Lahore, file) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: The Lahore High Court wants to know why Imran Khan's three sisters are still in custody.
Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi were detained in September, ahead of PTI's planned protest march to Islamabad on the twenty-seventh.
Aleema was detained on the twentieth of September. Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody a day later.
Lahore's deputy commissioner issued thirty-day detention orders under the public order law, citing police reports of a threat to public order.
A new petition, filed by Aleema's son, Shahrez Khan, says those orders expired on the nineteenth of October.
Yet, it says, the three women remain in Kot Lakhpat Jail, and are not wanted in any criminal case.
The petition argues that preventive detention cannot replace ordinary criminal law, and asks the court to order their release.
On Thursday, Justice Abher Gul Khan summoned Punjab's home secretary and the jail superintendent.
They must explain why the women are still held after their detention periods ended.
The court will hear the case again on the twenty-eighth of October.
No response from the Punjab government to the petition has been reported so far.
